solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Injury from kick aimed at player after three from Messi (8)

indicatorNotes.after: PASS is placed after TRES, so TRES comes first

blocks.note: Messi is Argentinian, and 'three' in Spanish is tres
a pass is a kick aimed at a teammate

annotation.surface: A footballer hurt by a kick meant for a teammate, just after Messi scored a hat-trick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Three from Messi' is the language Messi speaks, not a count of his goals. In law, a trespass is any wrongful act that injures someone, not only stepping on land.
annotation.definitionFit: In old legal and biblical usage a trespass is a wrong or injury done to another.

entries.clue: For puzzling last word, missing first letter (7)

indicatorNotes.missing first letter: says outright to drop the L at the front of LAST

blocks.note: LAST WORD without its first letter, L

annotation.surface: A crossword solver baffled by the final word of a puzzle that is missing its opening letter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For' opens the clue looking like a mere preposition leading in; it is the whole definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Money given for a cause is given towards it.

entries.clue: Time can be found reversing (3)

indicatorNotes.reversing: turns ARE round to read ERA

blocks.note: things that can be found ARE, in the sense of exist

annotation.surface: A claim that time can be found by going backwards.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter stretches 'can be found' to mean 'exist', as in 'there are wolves here': the plural verb ARE.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: an era is a span of history, one way of measuring time.

entries.clue: Oval filled at lunchtime, maybe pair batted incredibly (5,5)

indicatorNotes.incredibly: an incredible result is one scrambled beyond belief

annotation.surface: A cricket report: at the Oval ground at lunch, the batting pair had done amazingly well.
annotation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, and the whole clue is cricket until you see 'Oval' as a shape: a pitta is an oval flatbread split and filled for lunch.
annotation.definitionFit: A pitta is an oval flatbread often filled with salad or meat as a lunchtime sandwich; 'maybe' marks it as one example.

entries.clue: Fat root spliced in case of subsidence (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places WED within the case letters, the way something sits in a box
indicatorNotes.case of: the case of a word is its outside letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of subsidence
to get spliced is slang for to marry

annotation.surface: A thick tree root joined into the wall of a building to hold it up where the ground has sunk.
annotation.walkthrough: A swede is a large yellow-fleshed turnip, known as a rutabaga in North America.
annotation.definitionFit: A swede is a large swollen root vegetable.

entries.clue: Large section of church died apostate (6)

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels
the apse is the rounded end of a church
d. = died, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A big part of the church died out after abandoning its faith.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the last word, an adjective: a lapsed Catholic is one who has left the faith.
annotation.definitionFit: Lapsed describes someone who no longer practises their religion, as an apostate does.

entries.clue: Connect with answer yet? (4)

blocks.note: A = answer, as in Q and A
yet = but, as in 'small yet strong'

annotation.surface: An impatient question: has the answer clicked yet?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Connect with' reads like joining up with a person; here it is one plot of land touching another.
annotation.definitionFit: Things that abut meet and join at an edge.

entries.clue: Setting up funds, visit Washington, a friend having cased it (4,7)

indicatorNotes.having cased: PAL holds IT inside it like a case

blocks.note: to see a doctor is to visit one

annotation.surface: Advice for raising money: go to Washington and bring a friend who has checked the place out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cased' is the thieves' sense of scouting a place before a job, here it simply means holding inside, as a case holds its contents.
annotation.definitionFit: Seed capital is the money used to set up a new business.

entries.clue: Very scratched from stumble across dancer in club (7)

indicatorNotes.scratched from: V is struck out of the longer word, as a runner is scratched from a race

blocks.note: to stumble across something is to discover it

annotation.surface: A clubber got badly grazed after tripping over a dancer.
annotation.walkthrough: A discoer, one who goes to discos, is a rare word; it falls out of DISCOVER once V is gone.
annotation.definitionFit: A discoer is someone who dances at discos, the dance clubs.

entries.clue: A bit of woodwork irritated lawyers (8)

blocks.note: the Bar is the body of barristers

annotation.surface: Some carpentry annoyed the lawyers.
annotation.walkthrough: In football commentary 'the woodwork' means the goal frame, even though it is now metal; the crossbar is its top.
annotation.definitionFit: The crossbar is the horizontal part of the goal, one bit of what commentators call the woodwork.

entries.clue: With alien agitators on planet, show who’s boss (4,3,8)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, 'on' puts ET ROUSERS after EARTH

annotation.surface: With alien troublemakers landing on Earth, it is time to show them who is in charge.
annotation.walkthrough: The planet is a word to be written in, not the scene of an invasion.
annotation.definitionFit: To wear the trousers is to be the one in charge, traditionally in a household.

entries.clue: Cautious states led by king during revolt (4-6)

indicatorNotes.led by: to be led by someone is to walk behind them, so K goes in front of AVERS
indicatorNotes.during: what happens during an event sits inside its span of time, so KAVERS goes inside RISE

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly

annotation.surface: Nervous nations, headed by a king, in the middle of an uprising.
annotation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like countries; it is the verb, AVERS.
annotation.definitionFit: Risk-averse means unwilling to take chances, which is cautious.

entries.clue: Small point about retaining unpopular player performing badly for City (11)

indicatorNotes.retaining: S…PTON keeps OUT HAM inside it

blocks.note: a ham is an actor who overacts
on = about, as in 'a talk on birds'

annotation.surface: A little dig at a disliked footballer who played poorly for City.
annotation.walkthrough: The football surface makes 'player' a footballer; it is an actor. Southampton is a port city on England's south coast.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Southampton is one of England's cities, a port on the south coast.

entries.clue: Feature of cathedral music, probably also of the choir (4)

indicatorNotes.also of: says the answer is also part of the words that follow

annotation.surface: Something typical of music in a cathedral, and of its choir too.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is long and ends on 'probably': a cathedral's vast space usually makes sound echo.
annotation.definitionFit: Cathedrals are so cavernous that music sung in them usually echoes.

entries.clue: Be useful too, nag ordered girl (3,2,5)

indicatorNotes.ordered: the letters are put in a new order

annotation.surface: Nagging a girl to be helpful as well.
annotation.walkthrough: Something that would not go amiss would be welcome and useful.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: something that would not go amiss is welcome, so it helps out.

entries.clue: Team not finishing wine by itself (7)

annotation.surface: A team drinks wine on its own and does not finish it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By itself' reads as 'alone'; it is the arithmetic sense, a number multiplied by itself.
annotation.definitionFit: Maths sense: a squared number is one multiplied by itself, and the clue drops the word 'multiplied'.
annotation.definitionNote: 'by itself' is short for 'multiplied by itself'

entries.clue: Mud on ground covering island, time to get off (8)

indicatorNotes.ground: ground-up letters are broken and mixed
indicatorNotes.covering: a covering wraps round what it covers, so the rearranged letters wrap round IS

blocks.note: IS = island, placed after the D

annotation.surface: Mud on the ground around an island means it is time to climb down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ground' is the past participle of grind, not the earth underfoot.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: riders leave a horse or bicycle this way, stepping down from it.

entries.clue: Comic error putting half human on British throne (7)

indicatorNotes.half: 'half human' asks for half of a word for human: PERSON cut in two
indicatorNotes.putting: 'putting X on Y' is an instruction to place one piece next to another
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, PER goes after B LOO

blocks.note: the throne is a jokey name for the toilet, the loo

annotation.surface: A funny slip in which half a person was put on the British throne.
annotation.walkthrough: The royal throne is really a toilet; LOO is the British word.
annotation.definitionFit: A blooper is an embarrassing, funny mistake, especially one caught on film.

entries.clue: Judges again pardon separating parents (7)

indicatorNotes.separating: EH splits REARS into R and EARS

blocks.note: to rear children is to parent them
'Eh?' and 'Pardon?' both ask someone to repeat themselves

annotation.surface: A court reconsiders its pardon, splitting up a couple.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parents' is the verb (raises children), not mother and father; 'pardon' is the word you say when you have not heard.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal sense: a court hearing a case a second time is judging it again.

entries.clue: Archangel’s censure upset Jacob’s wife (7)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns LEAH upside down

blocks.note: Leah, Jacob's first wife in Genesis

annotation.surface: An archangel's rebuke upsets Jacob's wife.
annotation.walkthrough: Jacob married two sisters, Leah and Rachel; only Leah fits.
annotation.definitionFit: Raphael is one of the archangels named in scripture.

entries.clue: Twisted tootsie sounded OK (5-2)

indicatorNotes.sounded: the words are said out loud

blocks.note: wry = twisted, tootsie = a toe, in baby talk

annotation.surface: A twisted foot that was reported to be fine.
annotation.walkthrough: Right-oh is a cheerful British way of saying OK.
annotation.definitionFit: Right-oh is an informal British word of agreement, like OK.

entries.clue: Unlucky fellow rid of cold? Not so (7)

indicatorNotes.rid of: a man rid of a cold no longer has it, so CHAP no longer has its C

annotation.surface: An unfortunate man who thought he had shaken off his cold, but hadn't.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not so' reads as a denial; it is LESS, as in 'less happy' = 'not so happy'.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: hap is an old word for luck, so the hapless are without it.

entries.clue: Use machine to raise papa out of bed, taking minutes (4)

indicatorNotes.taking: UP takes M into itself, the way a house takes in a lodger

blocks.note: Papa is P in the phonetic alphabet
up = out of bed; its U comes first

annotation.surface: Using a machine to haul Dad out of bed, slowly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raise' belongs with the definition: to pump water is to raise it by machine.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the verb sense: water pumped from a well is raised by machine.

entries.clue: Batter on fish is rubbish (10)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, WALLOP goes after COD S

annotation.surface: A verdict on a fish-and-chip shop: the batter is awful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Batter' is the fish-shop coating in the surface but the verb 'hit' in the wordplay. Codswallop is British slang for nonsense.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang synonym: talk that is nonsense can be called either word.

entries.clue: Only five parts to decode (5)

indicatorNotes.parts: V parts SOLE, sitting between its letters

blocks.note: V is five in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: Just five pieces of a puzzle to crack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parts' reads as pieces; it is a verb, V parting SOLE.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: cracking a code or a crossword clue means working it out.

entries.clue: Gentle hits reflected fight that’s not serious (4)

indicatorNotes.reflected: a reflection shows the word back to front

annotation.surface: A few soft blows show the fight was never serious.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface nearly defines the answer twice: light taps are what a trivial spat involves.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a brief, petty quarrel is a squabble rather than a real fight.

entries.clue: Tea MP arranged with lieutenant with two more to come (15)

indicatorNotes.arranged: the letters are put in a new arrangement

annotation.surface: An MP's tea party organised alongside an army officer, with two more guests due.
annotation.walkthrough: Antepenultimate means third from last, so two more follow it.
annotation.definitionFit: The antepenultimate item is third from the end, with two more still to come.

entries.clue: Middle section of walk is circular part (3)

indicatorNotes.Middle section of: take the central letters of MARCH

blocks.note: to walk is to MARCH; drop its first and last letters

annotation.surface: The central stretch of a walk forms a loop.
annotation.walkthrough: The middle of 'walk' itself is AL, which leads nowhere: first turn walk into MARCH.
annotation.definitionFit: Geometry sense: a curved piece cut from a circle's edge is what the word names.

entries.clue: Biologist’s woolly article boring near the end (6)

indicatorNotes.boring: a drill boring into wood goes inside it, so AN goes inside LATE

blocks.note: late = near the end, as in late in the day

annotation.surface: A biologist's fleecy jumper, a dull thing near the end of its life.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' is not dull here but drilling: AN bores into LATE. Lanate is a technical word, hence 'Biologist's'.
annotation.definitionFit: Lanate is the biological term for woolly, covered in woolly hairs.

entries.clue: Hose between the sheets in Spooner’s aforementioned crate (8)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: aforementioned = said; its S sound swaps with the B of BOX
a crate is a box; with an S in front it becomes SOX, spelt SOCKS

annotation.surface: Stockings hidden in the bed inside a crate, as Spooner might describe it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hose' is stockings or socks, not a garden hosepipe; 'between the sheets' is simply in bed.
annotation.definitionFit: Bedsocks are socks worn in bed, so hosiery between the sheets.
